title: Base change, affineness of the source, and quasi-compactness and separatedness of affine morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Then: (1) for every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ the base change $X\times_YY'\to Y'$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]) is affine; (2) if $Y$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], then $X$ is affine; (3) $f$ is quasi-compact and separated, in particular quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; (4) a finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine.

source.place: Section Affine morphisms: Definition Tag 01S6 (morphisms-definition-affine; affine over an affine base: the preimage of the affine target is affine), Lemma Tag 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated, line 1721: an affine morphism is separated and quasi-compact), Lemma Tag 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine: base change); (4) a finite disjoint union $\coprod\operatorname{Spec}A_j=\operatorname{Spec}\prod A_j$ (the spectrum of a finite product of rings is the disjoint union of the spectra)
